## 449 · The branch guard's hook refused every commit made inside a rebase, because HEAD is detached there

**Enforced by:** GATE hub:branch-guard.mjs — the generated hook, when HEAD is detached, reads the rebase's own head-name record (`rebase-merge` or `rebase-apply`, found with `git rev-parse --git-path`) and judges that branch by the same work and promote rules; a rebase of any other branch, or of a detached HEAD, still falls through to the refusal
**Enforced by:** GATE hub:.githooks/pre-commit — the tracked hook is regenerated by `--install`, and the drift check reads that it matches `.branch-guard`

**Recorded 2026-11-01.** Measured on 31 October with a scratch harness of eight checks. A rebase whose exec step amends each commit makes a commit while HEAD is detached, and the hook knew a branch only by `HEAD`'s name, so it refused. The re-author of four local commits could not be done by the route the plan named. In the harness the old generator's hook refused a commit inside a rebase of `main`, the fault reproduced; the new hook accepted it, a plain commit on `main` was still accepted, a plain commit on another branch and a commit inside a rebase of another branch were still refused, a rebase of a detached HEAD was refused, and a rebase of a branch matching a glob in `work=` was accepted.

**What is done now.** The accept is bound to the record git keeps of which branch the rebase is rewriting, so it is as strict as the branch it names. Nothing about a rebase loosens a rule: the rebased branch must be one the repository allows commits on.

**What the change leaves.** No case was added to `session-guards.test.mjs`, since `branch-guard.mjs` is not one of its guard files; the harness lived in the scratchpad and the claim above is its reading.

**The general form.** A guard that identifies a context by one name fails in the states where git has not got that name. It asks git what the state is made of.
